a. 0.0003498

b. 235.4678

c. 70000.0

Give the number of significant figures in each of the following

a. \(1.230 \times 10^4\)

b. 0.002030

c. \(1.23 \times 10^4\)

_note: The book's item C refers back to item B by label alone. The four quantities are repeated in brackets so this row is answerable on its own on /browse, where a student sees one question at a time.

stem:
Find out the molar masses of the following compounds :

a. Copper sulphate crystal \((\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O})\)

b. Sodium carbonate, decahydrate \((\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O})\)

c. Mohr's salt \([\mathrm{FeSO_4(NH_4)_2SO_4 \cdot 6H_2O}]\)

(At. mass : Cu = 63.5; S = 32; O = 16; H = 1; Na = 23; C = 12; Fe = 56; N = 14)
bookAnswer: a. 249.5 g/mol; b. 286 g/mol; c. 392 g/mol

stem:
Work out the percentage composition of constituents elements in the following compounds :

a. Lead phosphate \([\mathrm{Pb_3(PO_4)_2}]\),

b. Potassium dichromate \((\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7})\),

c. Macrocosmic salt - Sodium ammonium hydrogen phosphate, tetrahydrate \((\mathrm{NaNH_4HPO_4 \cdot 4H_2O})\)

(At. mass : Pb = 207; P = 31; O = 16; K = 39; Cr = 52; Na = 23; N = 14)
_note: The atomic-mass list printed with this item omits H, which part (c) needs; H = 1 is supplied by the item directly above (D) and is standard. Noted, not silently patched.

stem: Find the percentage composition of constituent green vitriol crystals \((\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O})\). Also find out the mass of iron and the water of crystallisation in 4.54 kg of the crystals. (At. mass : Fe = 56; S = 32; O = 16)
bookAnswer: mass of Fe = 0.915 kg, mass of 7H2O = 2.058 kg

stem: The red colour of blood is due to a compound called "haemoglobin". It contains 0.335 % of iron. Four atoms of iron are present in one molecule of haemoglobin. What is its molecular weight ? (At. mass : Fe 55.84)
A substance, on analysis, gave the following percent composition: Na = 43.4 %, C = 11.3 % and O = 45.3 %. Calculate the empirical formula. (At. mass Na = 23 u, C = 12 u, O = 16 u).
Assuming the atomic weight of a metal M to be 56, find the empirical formula of its oxide containing 70.0% of M.
1.00 g of a hydrated salt contains 0.2014 g of iron, 0.1153 g of sulfur, 0.2301 g of oxygen and 0.4532 g of water of crystallisation. Find the empirical formula. (At. wt. : Fe = 56; S = 32; O = 16)
_note: Spans the p-11/p-12 column break: the stem begins in the right column of p-11 and completes at the head of the left column of p-12.

stem: An organic compound containing oxygen, carbon, hydrogen and nitrogen contains 20 % carbon, 6.7 % hydrogen and 46.67 % nitrogen. Its molecular mass was found to be 60. Find the molecular formula of the compound.
A compound on analysis gave the following percentage composition by mass : H = 9.09; O = 36.36; C = 54.55. Mol mass of compound is 88. Find its molecular formula.

Carbohydrates are compounds containing only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. When heated in the absence of air, these compounds decompose to form carbon and water. If 310 g of a carbohydrate leave a residue of 124 g of carbon on heating in absence of air, what is the empirical formula of the carbohydrate ?

Write each of the following in exponential notation :

a. 3,672,199

b. 0.000098

c. 0.00461

d. 198.75

Write each of the following numbers in ordinary decimal form :

a. \(3.49 \times 10^{-11}\)

b. \(3.75 \times 10^{-1}\)

c. \(5.16 \times 10^4\)

d. \(43.71 \times 10^{-4}\)

e. \(0.011 \times 10^{-3}\)

f. \(14.3 \times 10^{-2}\)

g. \(0.00477 \times 10^5\)

h. 5.00858585

Perform each of the following calculations. Round off your answers to three digits.

a. \((3.26\ 104)(1.54\ 106)\)

b. \((8.39\ 107)(4.53\ 109)\)

c. \(\dfrac{8.94 \times 10^6}{4.35 \times 10^4}\)

d. \(\dfrac{(9.28 \times 10^9)(9.9 \times 10^{-7})}{(511)(2.98 \times 10^{-6})}\)
_note: Parts a and b are transcribed EXACTLY as printed. Verified on the page at 5x magnification: the book prints '(3.26 104) (1.54 106)' and '(8.39 107) (4.53 109)' with BOTH the multiplication sign and the exponent superscripting lost — parts c and d on the same page set their exponents correctly, which is what identifies a and b as the defect. Carried to errata with the intended reading.

Part c is transcribed EXACTLY as printed. Verified at 5x: the second term reads '8.1 10^-4' with the multiplication sign dropped, while parts a, b and d on the same lines set theirs correctly. Carried to errata.

stem: A 1.000 mL sample of acetone, a common solvent used as a paint remover, was placed in a small bottle whose mass was known to be 38.0015 g. The following values were obtained when the acetone - filled bottle was weighed : 38.7798 g, 38.7795 g and 38.7801 g. How would you characterise the precision and accuracy of these measurements if the actual mass of the acetone was 0.7791 g ?

Your laboratory partner was given the task of measuring the length of a box (approx 5 in) as accurately as possible, using a metre stick graduated in milimeters. He supplied you with the following measurements:

12.65 cm, 12.6 cm, 12.65 cm, 12.655 cm, 126.55 mm, 12 cm.

a. State which of the measurements you would accept, giving the reason.

b. Give your reason for rejecting each of the others.

What weight of calcium oxide will be formed on heating 19.3 g of calcium carbonate ?

(At. wt. : Ca = 40; C = 12; O = 16)
_note: The atomic-mass line is printed as part of this item on p-13, indented beneath its stem — not as a preamble shared by the block. It is therefore carried in this row's own stem, so the row is self-contained before commit.

stem: The hourly energy requirements of an astronaut can be satisfied by the energy released when 34 grams of sucrose are "burnt" in his body. How many grams of oxygen would be needed to be carried in space capsule to meet his requirement for one day ?
